seven_q.Q0_posture: Analytical and integrative; seeks to demonstrate structural convergence between empirical science and theological doctrine
seven_q.Q1_identity: An isomorphism record establishing a structural mapping between addiction neuroscience and the theology of sin bondage
seven_q.Q2_domain: Interdisciplinary: neuroscience, theology, philosophy of mind, recovery studies
seven_q.Q3_claim: Addiction and sin bondage share a common topological structure of progressive enslavement in closed systems requiring external intervention for liberation
seven_q.Q4_support: 10 independent correspondences (tolerance, allostatic load, withdrawal, neural entrenchment, self-rescue impossibility, external intervention, relapse, cross-tolerance, dopamine hijacking/idolatry, recovery community/ecclesiology) plus empirical evidence from neuroscience and pastoral theology
seven_q.Q5_dependencies: ISO-002 (Terminus Sui), ISO-003 (Entropy/Sin), empirical data on addiction, theological doctrine of sin and grace
seven_q.Q6_consequences: Forces recognition that recovery and sanctification share structural requirements; constrains models of sin (cannot be purely volitional) and addiction (cannot be purely chemical)
seven_q.Q7_kill: Demonstration that addicts can reliably self-rescue through willpower alone; demonstration that tolerance reverses spontaneously in closed systems; demonstration that solitary recovery works as well as community-supported recovery
